content.text: The renewal terms match our preferred position on every parameter, and no conflicting uplift or renewal language exists elsewhere.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
input.rationale: § 8.2 provides automatic renewals of only twelve months (no multi-year auto-renewal), a Customer opt-out on just thirty days' written notice (well inside the ≤30-day preferred window), and a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal — with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which is better than our preferred ask. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI and three percent, matching the preferred cap, requires ninety days' notice of any increase (a Vendor obligation running in our favour, not a notice burden on us), and bars increases on prepaid periods. The only renewal/uplift language in the document sits in §§ 8.2–8.3; § 2.2 lets an Order Form prevail only for that Order Form and only where it expressly identifies the conflicting provision, so no renewal or price-increase term can be slipped into an Order Form silently. Preferred position met in full; no redline needed.
